roadmap.goal: Story 6459 (T1): the backend test run keeps its memory flat. Disposed test hosts are released instead of being pinned by static timers. Two roots are removed: (1) the OAuth providers hold a factory-made HTTP client for the life of the host, which keeps the client factory's cleanup timer looping; (2) the rate limiters' replenishment timers are never stopped when the host is disposed (the one-address global limiter, and the framework middleware's private endpoint limiter). Rate limiting stays ON with the same rules. A leak guard in the test project (cases A, B, C) fails if a disposed host stays reachable. Target (the only one): peak memory of a full standard-filter run under 3 GB and flat, measured before and after by the lead.

phases.name: Release disposed test hosts: OAuth per-request clients, then the rate-limiter seam and the leak guard
phases.description: One slice, two serial steps (01-01 then 01-02), owned by the crafter, profile standard, in the main checkout. Preconditions P0, P-final and the closing mutation run are owned by the lead (see roadmap preconditions). Measured in DESIGN: neither the OAuth change nor the rate-limiter change frees any host alone, so 01-01 turns no leak-guard case green and ALL [Ignore] attributes on TestHostIsReleasedAfterDisposeTest (cases A, B, C) come off together in 01-02, the first change that frees a host. The guard fixture and its allowlist entry in BackendTestParallelizationGuardTest are already committed (DISTILL). Nothing is pushed. Each commit is focused and green on its own; refactor commits are separate from feature commits. Git commands prefixed LEAN_CTX_DISABLED=1. Run only the filtered test classes named per step; the full standard-filter run belongs to the lead. Standard filter: TestCategory!=Integration&TestCategory!=JiraIntegration&TestCategory!=LinearIntegration&TestCategory!=AdoIntegration&TestCategory!=ServiceNowIntegration. Rules for all code in both steps: (a) comments are rare, written for a stranger, and never cite internal references (no story, decision, ADR, slice or scenario ids such as D1b, A2, ADR-005, AC-5.2); the reason goes in plain language or in the commit body. (b) No nWave scenario tags in code or test names (no @us-, @slice-, @kpi-, @contract-shape, @walking_skeleton, @driving_port, @error, @real-io); test names are plain language. (c) Read docs/ci-learnings.md (backend section) before writing code; the build promotes Sonar and Roslyn rules to errors, so `dotnet build` must finish with zero warnings. (d) The ArchUnit rules in the test project must stay green. (e) The product-side behaviour of routes, DTOs, responses and rate-limit rules is unchanged.

steps.name: OAuth providers ask IHttpClientFactory per request; test hosts shorten the handler lifetime
steps.description: Commit type: `fix(oauth): ask the HTTP client factory per token request instead of holding a client`. Change JiraOAuthProvider and AdoOAuthProvider so the constructor takes IHttpClientFactory (the client name constant HttpClientName is already public on each class) instead of an HttpClient, and each token request asks the factory for the named client at the point of use. Do not dispose the client in a way that disposes the pooled handler (the factory owns the handler). Change the two singleton registrations in Lighthouse.Backend/Lighthouse.Backend/Program.cs (around lines 1526-1542) into plain type registrations (AddSingleton<JiraOAuthProvider>() style, resolved through the container); leave the AddHttpClient(name, 30 s timeout) registrations (around 356-364) and the 2-minute product handler lifetime (around 340-343) untouched. Arrange-only test edits (assertions unchanged): JiraOAuthProviderTest.CreateProvider, AdoOAuthProviderTest.CreateProvider and OAuthServiceTest.ArrangeRefreshThroughARealIdentityProvider each build a Mock<IHttpClientFactory> whose CreateClient(<Provider>.HttpClientName) returns a fresh `new HttpClient(handler, disposeHandler: false)` on every call (a function, not a shared instance; disposeHandler:false so one request's `using` cannot dispose the stub handler the next request needs) and pass factory.Object. In OAuthServiceTest the handler is the real identity provider; RequestCountingHandler assertions stay. No new shared helper. In Lighthouse.Backend/Lighthouse.Backend.Tests/TestHelpers/TestWebApplicationFactory.cs add a test-only re-registration of the client factory's handler lifetime to 1 second (ConfigureAll<HttpClientFactoryOptions> applied after the product's registration) with a plain-language comment on why (a host that really used a client stays pinned until the lifetime plus the factory's fixed 10 s cleanup tick; no test relies on connection reuse). This step turns NO leak-guard case green; report that as measured, do not claim otherwise, and do not remove any [Ignore] here. Gates: `dotnet build` with 0 warnings; run only the three OAuth classes (filter FullyQualifiedName~JiraOAuthProviderTest|FullyQualifiedName~AdoOAuthProviderTest|FullyQualifiedName~OAuthServiceTest) plus the OAuth controller and registry tests, and record the passed/failed counts per class.

steps.name: Test hosts run without rate limiting unless a fixture tests it; leak guard enabled
steps.description: Commit type: `fix(test-infra): run test hosts without rate limiting unless a fixture tests it`. Maintainer decision (2026-11-01, in chat) replaces the reflection seam: product code for rate limiting stays exactly as it is (`app.UseRateLimiter()` under the existing `RateLimits:Enabled` gate, the global limiter unchanged). (1) In Lighthouse.Backend/Lighthouse.Backend.Tests/TestHelpers/TestWebApplicationFactory.cs set `RateLimits:Enabled` to false by default for every test host, with a short plain-language comment: a host with the rate limiters on stays reachable after disposal (their refill timers capture it), so the bulk of tests run without them; fixtures that test rate limiting switch it back on. (2) Find every fixture that tests rate limiting (at least S6_RateLimitingTests, UsageDataConsentRateLimitTests, Slice11CastAVoteScenarios, UsageDataEventCeilingTests; ctx_search for 429, TooManyRequests, RateLimit, RateLimits in the test project to find any others) and make each opt in to `RateLimits:Enabled=true` for its own hosts, in the way the fixture already configures its host (UseSetting / in-memory configuration). Assertions unchanged. (3) Add one test (in TestHostIsReleasedAfterDisposeTest or next to it) that a default test host runs without rate limiting, so the default cannot silently flip back. (4) In TestHostIsReleasedAfterDisposeTest.cs remove ALL THREE [Ignore] attributes (A, B, C); leave assertions as written; case C relies on 01-01's one-second handler lifetime. If a case is not green, stop and report the printed failure. (5) Update the guard's comments/messages that name the rate limiters' timers so they describe the new situation (default hosts run without rate limiting; a host with it on is expected to stay reachable). (6) Stryker config docs/feature/story-6459-t1-backend-test-memory-flat/mutation/stryker-config.story-6459.json: remove the RateLimiterOwner glob and filter term; mutate only the two provider files. (7) Gates with counts: `dotnet build` 0 warnings; every rate-limit fixture found in (2) green; the three OAuth classes green; the guard fixture 5 consecutive `dotnet test -c Release --filter FullyQualifiedName~TestHostIsReleasedAfterDisposeTest` runs, alone, each recorded; detailed-log evidence that the NonParallelizable fixture ran alone; the two BackendTestParallelizationGuardTest tests; no `[Ignore` left in the fixture. (8) Record in feature-delta.md under `## Wave: DELIVER / [REF] Evidence step 01-02`: the list of opted-in fixtures and how found, the counts, the five Release runs and the exclusivity evidence. Never run the unfiltered suite; never run another backend suite concurrently.
